statement: Coverage of the same Goldman note reports hyperscalers would need roughly $300 billion of annual AI revenue to break even on these outlays, and that more than a third of 2027 AI investment is expected to be debt-funded.
why: Spending that leans on borrowing is far more sensitive to credit conditions and to whether AI revenue actually shows up, which is where a demand air pocket would start.

impact.mechanism: If over a third of the build is debt-financed against a $300 billion revenue break-even, tighter credit or slower AI revenue would force capex cuts that hit accelerator orders first.

evidence.excerpt: the hyperscalers would need annual AI revenues of roughly $300 billion to break even on these outlays, and that more than a third of 2027 AI investment is expected to be debt-funded

confidence.basis: Secondary summary of other outlets' coverage of the same note, read inside a single document; no credit terms or current spreads given.

entity: Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Oracle, Meta (top-5 US hyperscalers); Goldman Sachs (forecaster)
